questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Personally I have friends in Korea and started learning korean and wanting to go to Korea when I was 15 years old. So it has been a long time coming dream of mine to go.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was just such a fun, interesting, beautiful country and I had an absolutely amazing time.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a little bit hard at first because English is not their first language. But if you download naver to find your way and get a T-money card in a convenience store for the trains and busses you are on your way. Also you need to buy a telephone subscription to get data (you can do it, in the airport)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot to be honest. I was lucky my landlord and my roomies were very helpfull. We just figured it out along the way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I went too SKKU in seoul and and it was fine. I could really have used some kinds of social arrangements to introduce and meet other students. It was kind of hard to make friends at school. But I managed and got good friends there as well.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived with "simple spaces" in Haebangchon area (close to Itawon). It was cheap, I lived with two roommates and I really recommend the area and the landlords. The landlords also did cultural and party trips you could sign up for which was nice. I really recommend simple spaces. But! choose the haebangchon area - I know other people weren't as happy with the housing in other areas.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its the best way to live! There are a lot of rules (curfews, gender division, no guest allowed) in the dormitories or other ways of living. People were not that happy with it from my experience. Rent an apartment! If you do it quick (4 months before arriving) a lot of places are free.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very happy with the housing in simple spaces!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The landlords just guided me throuh it - but they were from the USA living in seoul so communication was easy. My other friends had a hard time communicating with their korean landlords.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At SKKU university you had to choose your courses at the same time online internationally. I did not get all the courses I wanted and all my 30 ects points. But when ariving at the first week of uni you can go to the professors and ask if you can join their courses - and a lot of them will help you. Just keep trying!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, so you have to do it in person if you want courses you missed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: got 3/5 of my wants. Then I pleaded with my teacher and got two other courses as well. So it was good

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: look at the other boxes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: SKKu was a fine uni. A lot of international students. The courses was a lot easier to follow than in Denmark - but I have heard that about almost every exchange experience.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I could choose freely kind of which was nice.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very much like reminded me of Danish gymnasium style. You get credits for attendance, your powerpoint presentations and you have midterms and finals. I found it easier than in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1.Comparative Thought and Culture: Horizons East and West 
2. Contemporary Korean Society & Culture 
3. Political & Economic Development in Korea 
4. Popular Culture and Digital Media
5. Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights was interesting if you study social sciences. Also I think Contemporary Korean Society & Culture is a good introduction to korean society.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: They wanted me to pay for a korean national health care insurance every month (140kr). It was an awful experience to get out of it - they did not think my travel insurance was good enough. I ended up not paying it and they did not give me a ticket or anything so I recommend just ignoring it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food is less expensive than in copenhagen. You can buy a good cheap meal for 10.000 won (50 dkk). And the convenience store kimbabs are also good and filling for lunch.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were not allowed to join the dance team:(

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: not a lot unfortunatly. I know they made kimchi one day which people thought was very fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go clubbing, go traveling out of seoul, go skiing, go to the movies and go to local food and clothing markets! (dongdaemun jewelry market and dongmye clothing market, and gwanjang food marked)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on trips with your friends! go shopping, and to cafes and enjoy the good weather!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: difficult at first. It is a lot different than Denmark. I would recommend to learn the korean alphabet and how to say "hello, goodbye, thank you, the food is delicious and how much is this". A lot of Koreans do not speak English so learn as much korean as you can.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it was exstreamly difficult because I only had subjects and classes with international students. I got one korean friend by random there, but it was very hard.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't know actually. Maybe that people can get mad at you, old people. Sometimes they yell at you and get annoyed. Dont take it personally.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Koreans are so warm and funny and interactive if you just try to speak their language. And there is just so much fun things to do in seoul - it is an amazing city when you young!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. try to be social in the beguinning to get friends
2. go out and do things and remember to travel to smaller cities
3. be active when your at uni, but live your life and do stuff when your not there

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: oij! remember to go to jimjilbangs! korean saunas are the best.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just the people you meet (other exchange students) and the relationships you build together

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I felt a little lonely sometimes but its a natural part of it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: just go to seoul - its a once in a life time experience and so much more interesting than going to a european country you will go to many times in your life. Dont be scared it is a amazing country and culture and people with a crazy history.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
